decisions.reason: The spout was already required to face the baristas, and its separately accepted stainless-steel render-matching design is already represented by a same-message MODIFY; moving the placard does not further change it.
Moving and orienting the placard does not change the established beige body or green accent colors.
The placard relocation and customer-facing orientation do not alter bowl capacity, depth, geometry, or enclosure-size constraints.
The source changes the placard's placement rather than the enclosure's thickness, overall size, or accommodation of the bowl wells.
Placard placement and viewing orientation do not change the splash-control target.
The source does not change mixing quality, foam consistency, whisk geometry, or whisk style.
The placard decision does not alter the dispensing path's removability, flushing, or cleaning requirements.
The source contains no necessary change to the BOM deliverable or its recorded whisk selection.
The placard relocation does not change the established gravity feed, valve behavior, dripping constraint, or controlled-flow behavior.
Placard placement has no effect on the required spout connection or bowl-bottom sealing behavior.
The source does not modify the requirement to prevent liquid from entering the base or electrical components.
Moving the placard does not change the prototype's off-the-shelf electronics strategy.
